app.title: TissuePlex: cell-cell communication on the tissue image
app.summary: The person picks a spatial dataset and an edge set, and the tissue image opens with layers that can be switched on: transcript dots, cell outlines and directed cell-to-cell communication edges. They narrow the view by unchecking genes and signalling mechanisms, filtering cells or edges by a metadata column, and colouring cells or edges by gene-set score or by an annotation. Clicking a cell or an edge opens its details, including the cells it connects to and every mechanism with its score. Two panels can be set side by side to compare areas, datasets or edge sets. They can draw regions to export the selected cells as a CSV, measure distances, and frame a high-resolution figure to export as a PNG.

task.text: Explore which cells signal to which across a tissue section, through which ligand-receptor mechanisms, and export cell selections and figures.

data.text: A spatial transcriptomics dataset (a morphology image, cell or spot outlines, transcript positions and per-cell metadata) with a directed graph between cells that has one score for each ligand-receptor mechanism on each edge.
data.item: a cell (or spot or bin) on the tissue section, and a directed edge between two cells with its scored mechanisms

stage.text: exploring inferred cell-cell communication on the tissue after it has been scored, before writing up figures

mechanism.text: A pan-and-zoom tissue image carries vector layers for transcripts, cell outlines and directed edges. A sidebar of toggles, filters, colour-by menus and legends drives what is drawn. Clicking a cell or edge opens a floating detail panel, and a second linked panel can be opened for side-by-side comparison.

field.text: cell-cell communication inferred from spatial transcriptomics, in biology

workflow.name: explore a spatial graph laid over an image, then export selections and figures

steps.here: Pick a dataset from the folder of instrument outputs, whose platform is detected automatically. If there is more than one edge set, pick one, and choose a morphology channel.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The tissue image pans and zooms, with layers for transcript dots, cell outlines and directed edges with arrowheads, plus autocrine rings. Each layer has a toggle, an opacity and a sampling density.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Uncheck gene species or ligand-receptor mechanisms, either by hand or by importing a list CSV. Filter cells, sending or receiving endpoints, or edges by one metadata column, using categories or a value range.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Colour cells by a gene-set expression score and edges by their summed score over the visible mechanisms, or colour either by a metadata column. Legends can be clamped and low values faded.

Clicking a cell shows its metadata and its unfiltered neighbourhood: connected cells, the enclosing radius, the mix of cell types and the top mechanisms. Clicking an edge lists every active mechanism with its score, along with any annotations.
Split into two panels, each with its own dataset, edge set and rotation. A Match button moves one panel to the other's view.
Draw a polygon region and download its cells as a CSV, or frame a rectangle and export a figure at a chosen size and DPI with a scale bar. Save PNG captures the screen.

distinctive: Edges are directed and carry many scored mechanisms each. Toggling a mechanism recomputes every edge's colour from only the mechanisms still visible.
Self-signalling is drawn as a ring on each cell, on the same colour scale and mechanism filter as the edges.
A clicked cell's neighbourhood ignores the viewport, sampling and filters, so it reflects the whole tissue rather than what is on screen.
Readers for several instrument platforms convert each one to the same pixel space. The interface relabels itself (cell, spot or bin) and hides layers a platform cannot serve.
Annotation tables dropped into a folder beside the data become colour-by and filter options without changing the source files.
